text:
alice.sales: Heads-up — Customer Nimbus wants to run a week-long POC for Redwood Private in their AWS account. Architecture ask: dual-homed TGW attachment (two AZs), outbound egress through their F5 with TLS inspection. They need us to confirm PrivateLink vs NAT public egress tradeoffs and any cert/pinning blockers.
ben.netops: TL;dr: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) avoids public egress entirely, but requires the customer to accept our interface endpoint service in their account and open SGs. If they insist on going via their F5 for inspection, we'll need stable egress IPs and a bypass plan for pinned certs.
alice.sales: They specifically asked about firewall rules they should open. Also price ask: will Dedicated/reserved affect egress handling? They want an estimate to include in the SOW.
dan.se: For the POC we usually recommend two options: 1) PrivateLink (no internet egress) — easiest for security review; 2) VPC-to-VPC via TGW with NAT egress — gives them control but needs static egress IPs. Dedicated capacity doesn't change network requirements, but Dedicated can be deployed into a private VPC where we can terminate to interface endpoints. Pricing: Dedicated includes predictable reserved cost; egress bandwidth is still subject to cloud/provider data transfer — we'll call that out separately in the quote.
claire.security: Important security note: TLS inspection in the middle will break certificate pinning and some mutual-TLS flows (e.g., if the customer pins certs to our model endpoints). If their platform intercepts TLS and re-signs, we need either: a) explicit bypass for model hostnames, or b) use PrivateLink so traffic never leaves the AWS network.
ben.netops: Sample firewall/security group allowlist snippet for PrivateLink option:
```
# Security Group on customer side for interface endpoint -> allow outbound to our endpoint service
Type: TLS  Protocol: TCP  Port: 443  Destination: com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx
# If they go NAT/egress route, allow outbound to these hostnames/IPs on 443
Hostnames: api.redwood.com, model-prod.redwood-inference.internal
Egress IPs: <we will provide static egress IPs or ranges>
```
alice.sales: Can we commit to providing the static egress IPs before the POC kickoff? Customer's procurement needs a CIDR to whitelist for scheduled firewall changes.
dan.se: We can provide a small set of stable egress IPs if they use our NAT/egress egress-proxy (requires Dedicated or Private with our egress appliance). For hosted (shared) instances we cannot guarantee static IPs. I can produce the egress IP list if they sign the POC addendum.
claire.security: Also add to security questionnaire: "Will any TLS interception be performed by customer-managed middleboxes for Redwood traffic?" If yes, require a list of hostnames/ports to be bypassed.
alice.sales: Action items for presales doc: 1) provide a one-pager comparing PrivateLink vs TGW+NAT for POC (include firewall snippet), 2) conditional egress IP list and pre-POC checklist, 3) line item in SOW about egress bandwidth estimate. I'll draft and loop legal for the addendum.
ben.netops: FYI — if they choose TGW+NAT we should also recommend health-check path and keepalive rules so the long-lived websocket/streaming sessions don't get killed by the F5. Typical keepalive: 60s.
infra-bot: deploy:created pcap-handoff 1728004000 for Nimbus POC staging vpc (for internal debugging).
alice.sales: Thanks all — I'll send the initial presales doc this afternoon. Claire, Dan: can you review the checkbox on cert bypass language before EOD? :crossed_fingers:
claire.security: On it, will add suggested language for bypass and mutual-TLS exceptions.
dan.se: Will add the egress IP options and a small config snippet for TGW route tables.
alice.sales: Closing the thread for now unless someone has more network blockers.
